text:
Alex: quick heads-up — rolled a quantized v2 reranker to staging. seeing MRR +3.9% but NDCG@10 down -2.4%. odd split, same holdout.
Priya: whoa. any config changes besides quant?
Alex: only 4-bit PTQ + our new tokenizer whitespace normalization patch i landed yesterday (strip repeated spaces). sampling/order code also got a tiny change in candidate shuffle seed.
Dan: do you have the eval command & config? paste here pls.
Alex: sure — ran
```
./eval_rerank --model=ranker-v2-ptq4 --holdout=2024-01-01 --k=10 --shuffle-seed=42 --norm=whitespace_strip
```
and metric output (staging snapshot):
```
MRR@10: 0.214 -> 0.222 (+3.9%)
NDCG@10: 0.512 -> 0.499 (-2.4%)
```
Mei: small drop but statistically significant? p-values? CI overlap?
Alex: quick bootstrap: delta ndcg -0.013, 95% CI [-0.021, -0.004] -> looks real. mrr delta CI doesn't overlap bad side.
Priya: could be candidate ordering interacting with whitespace_norm. if top-relevance docs had trailing multiple spaces in source and normalization removed anchor tokens that model used. weird but possible.
Dan: can you repro with the old tokenizer and new quant? and vice versa? split the factors.
Alex: running 4 experiments now: (A) old tok + FP32, (B) old tok + PTQ4, (C) new tok + FP32, (D) new tok + PTQ4. will post results. ETA ~30m.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for staging-eval job #8821 (Alex).
Mei: also check candidate ordering stable sort vs shuffle change — if sampling changed candidate priors, ndcg sensitive to rank positions. maybe mrr benefits because top-1 got better but tail positions worse.
Priya: good point. add a control where we fix candidate ordering to canonical (by doc-id).
Dan: also capture score distribution histograms and per-query delta buckets (short vs long queries). run slice: query_len<8, >=8.
Alex: results — quick summary (from staging-eval #8821):
```
A oldtok FP32:   MRR 0.218 NDCG 0.513
B oldtok PTQ4:   MRR 0.219 NDCG 0.512
C newtok FP32:   MRR 0.216 NDCG 0.506
D newtok PTQ4:   MRR 0.223 NDCG 0.495
```
So biggest ndcg drop is when both newtok and PTQ4 are present. PTQ alone negligible. newtok FP32 also down but smaller.
Mei: looks additive. that points to tokenizer change shifting tokenization around quant-sensitive layers (embedding lookup indices change -> small activation distribution shifts magnified by PTQ).
Priya: can we try PTQ calibration with representative tokenization (i.e., using newtok docs) instead of old calibration corpora? maybe quant was calibrated on oldtok outputs.
Alex: yea recalibrating now with corpus processed by new tokenizer. quick run: re-run PTQ calibrate -> deploy eval.
Dan: while that's running, can you check per-query topk rank swap stats? like how many queries had top1 change and how that correlates with ndcg loss.
Alex: pulled small table: top1 changes up for 7.8% queries (these mostly drive MRR up). but ndcg loss concentrated in queries with >3 relevant items where rank of relevant items moved down.
Priya: hypothesis: new tokenizer merges a common punctuation token leading to shorter input and different context windows; model then weighs different spans. combined with quant rounding leads to subtle score shifts.
Mei: if recalibration fixes it, we pin newtok + PTQ4 but retrain quant moments. if not, maybe revert whitespace normalization and try a less aggressive rule (collapse >3 spaces -> single, keep double).
Alex: recalibration finished: D' (newtok + PTQ4 recalibrated) -> MRR 0.224 NDCG 0.507. improvement vs D but ndcg still -0.006 vs baseline. CI now crosses zero? CI [-0.014, +0.002].
Dan: ok that suggests calibration was major factor. remaining delta is small. we should run longer eval (more bootstrap samples) and a production-like candidate ordering test.
Priya: agree. also add a human inspection sample for queries where ndcg drop >0.05 — check if formatting change removed cues.
Alex: will do. queued a canary: 5% traffic with newtok+PTQ4 recalibrated + canonical ordering. monitor ndcg/MRR, latency, p99.
infra-bot: canary rollout started (canary-id 6734) -> traffic 5%.
Mei: nice. keep an eye on error logs and scoring outliers.
Alex: thanks all — will update thread once canary stabilizes or if human review flags systemic issues. :thumbsup:
Priya: cheers, thanks for the thorough split tests.
Dan: thx, good triage.
